punchline: A professor who'd worked in the same building for twenty-five years found the nearest fire extinguisher inches from his own doorknob.
thirty_sec: A hardworking first-year gets a D on his psychology test. He went to every lecture, highlighted the book, and reread his highlighted notes until everything felt familiar. What he never did was test himself. Make It Stick points to studies where rereading in a row gave no benefit at all. Familiarity feels like knowing. Closing the book and trying to recall is what actually shows you, and builds, what you know.
